topic: 30-second Chinese introduction to Pi, grounded in https://pi.dev/docs/latest
research_summary: Pi is an extensible terminal AI agent, not a particular model: give it a working folder and a goal, then it can inspect files, run commands, edit content and complete multi-step work. The strongest 30-second introduction should demonstrate that concrete loop, then show model choice and extensibility. Current official documentation and the Pi 1.0 announcement supersede prevalent four-tools/no-MCP narratives: 1.0 includes Codemode with native MCP. No speed, cost-saving or benchmark superiority claim was independently established. A safety qualifier is important because project trust is not an execution sandbox. Audience and platform were not specified; developer-oriented Chinese narration is a proposal assumption, not a confirmed user preference.

data_points.claim: Pi works in the terminal and can inspect files, run commands, edit content and work through multi-step tasks from a goal and working folder.

The official quickstart uses four setup stages: install, start in a working folder, choose a model, and give Pi a task. Sessions save automatically and pi --continue resumes the latest session for that folder.
Model connections include supported subscriptions, API keys, local GGUF models through a llama.cpp router, and compatible endpoints; /model selects among available authenticated models.
TypeScript extensions can add executable tools, commands, event handlers, providers, session state and terminal UI; instructions alone are handled by lighter customization mechanisms.
Pi 1.0 includes Codemode with native MCP support, virtual-model extension support, deferred tool loading and a full-screen default interface.
Pi tools and extensions run with the permissions of the Pi process; project trust does not sandbox tool execution and Pi does not request approval before every tool call.

misconceptions.myth: Pi is a model or Raspberry Pi hardware.
misconceptions.reality: This Pi is an extensible terminal agent that connects to a model provider.

misconceptions.myth: Pi still has no native MCP support.
misconceptions.reality: Official Pi 1.0 explicitly introduces Codemode with native MCP support; older tutorials are historical.

misconceptions.myth: Trusting a project or selecting a working folder confines execution to that folder.
misconceptions.reality: Project trust governs resource loading, not an OS sandbox. Use actual isolation for untrusted work.
